title: tenant-fanout-affinity-latency-skew-remediation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported sustained TTFT regressions and drop in tokens/sec for long-session workloads (session length > 512 tokens). The effect was visible across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments but manifested differently per-tenant: some tenants saw 3-6x first-token latency for fanout requests while others saw throughput collapse on multi-model requests. Alerting fired March 10 08:22 UTC. This ticket tracks the triage, hot mitigation, root-cause fix and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate 75 concurrent sessions with average prompt length 600 tokens against model-variants A/B/C using multiplex routing
Enable session-affinity hashing at router level (stateful routing on) with churned backend pool
Observe initial token latency increase and tokens/sec drop within 30s of sustained load
Reproduce in hosted region eu-west-1, in a dedicated pool (cust-reserved) and a private VPC cluster to confirm cross-deployment impact
investigation_summary: Investigations pointed to transiently increased fanout on certain tenants. The router's affinity hashing change (rolled three days prior) increased cross-shard fanout for sessions that spanned model-variant probing. That change degraded KV-cache locality and forced frequent kernel rebinds across GPUs in heterogenous pools, increasing setup overhead and causing token throughput collapse and elevated TTFT. Differences across hosted/dedicated/private were due to pool heterogeneity and pinned model variants in Dedicated and Private customers.
mitigation_taken: 03-10 09:05 UTC: Rolled back router affinity change to stable hash v1.2.17 -> immediate reduction in fanout observed
03-10 09:20 UTC: Deployed emergency rate-shepherd on affected tenant routes to limit parallel probe concurrency to 2
03-10 10:00 UTC: For Dedicated pools, temporarily pinned requests to local model replicas to preserve KV cache locality
03-11 14:30 UTC: Gradual canary rollout of affinity-guard in runtime with assertion checks against fanout > 1.5x baseline
root_cause: A subtle regression in the new affinity hashing algorithm increased cross-shard distribution for sessions that included model probing and variant fallbacks. This non-local routing caused repeated KV cache misses and required repinning of kernels across heterogenous GPUs, adding setup latency per-token and collapsing tokens/sec under sustained load.
next_steps: 01. Add a fanout anomaly detector with tenant-scoped alerts (P1)
02. Add unit/regression tests for affinity hashing that simulate heterogenous pool topologies (P0)
03. Evaluate safer canary policy: gradual traffic reweighting + realtime KV-miss telemetry gating (P0)
04. Document operational runbook for tenant fanout incidents and share with SRE/SE teams (P1)
rollback_plan: If unexpected regressions appear in the affinity-guard canary, restore router to v1.2.17 and re-apply tenant pinning. Ensure all impacted customers are notified via status page and account SRE.
customer_communication: 03-10 11:00 UTC: Initial 'investigating' status update posted to status.redwood.com
03-10 12:45 UTC: Follow-up for affected enterprise contacts with mitigation steps and ETA for full recovery
03-11 16:00 UTC: Post-incident summary sent to impacted customers with temporary workarounds and timeline to permanent fix
follow_up_tasks: Instrument per-tenant KV-cache hit-rate in Console with retention 90d
Add traffic-proportional per-tenant canary throttles to Dedicated autopilot
Run chaos tests that change pool heterogeneity during heavy fanout to validate routing resilience
notes: Measured improvement after rollback: median TTFT reduced from 480ms -> 120ms for affected sessions in hosted eu-west-1
Tokens/sec recovered from ~12 tok/s -> ~210 tok/s for long sessions after tenant-pin/rebind mitigation in Dedicated pools
Private deployments required coordinated customer-side redeploy for pinning; SRE worked with 2 customers to expedite
